quarterly_data.signal: 20-F full-year 2025 results: net sales were EUR 43,626 million, up 6.2% reported and 9.9% at constant exchange rates (2024: EUR 41,081 million), all in the single Biopharma segment. Dupixent sales reached EUR 15,714 million (+20.2%, +25.2% CER; United States EUR 11,538 million) and launches EUR 5,721 million (+29.1%, +34.0% CER); by region the United States contributed EUR 22,176 million (+16.3% CER), Europe EUR 9,169 million and the Rest of the World EUR 12,281 million (China EUR 2,621 million, +2.0% CER). Business operating income was EUR 12,149 million (+7.1%, +11.9% CER), 27.8% of net sales; R&D expenses were EUR 7,842 million; impairment of intangible assets rose to EUR 2,241 million (EUR 248 million in 2024); net income of EUR 7,851 million included EUR 2,874 million from discontinued operations (Opella, with a EUR 2,718 million gain on disposal). In the 20-F's table of acquisitions and capitalized interest, 2025 acquisitions were EUR 1,822 million (all Biopharma), of which Manufacturing & Supply EUR 1,157 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 net sales EUR 43,626 million (+6.2%, +9.9% CER); Dupixent EUR 15,714 million; launches EUR 5,721 million; BOI EUR 12,149 million (27.8% of net sales); acquisitions EUR 1,822 million (Manufacturing & Supply EUR 1,157 million)

quarterly_data.signal: The 20-F pipeline tables report the 2025 clinical readouts: venglustat met the primary endpoints of the LEAP2MONO phase 3 study in Gaucher disease type 3 (February 2026), with Sanofi to pursue global regulatory filings, but did not meet the primary endpoint of the PERIDOT phase 3 study in Fabry disease (a reduction in neuropathic and abdominal pain was observed; CARAT ongoing); efdoralprin alfa met the primary endpoint of the ElevAATe phase 2 study in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency emphysema; Dupixent met the primary endpoint of the LIBERTY-AFRS-AI phase 3 study in allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (then under US priority review); Sarclisa's subcutaneous formulation met the primary endpoints of its phase 3 studies in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (under review in the US, the EU, Japan and China); and Fluzone HD showed positive safety and immunogenicity results at a phase 3 interim analysis in adults aged 50+. Setbacks: Rezurock's first-line chronic graft versus host disease phase 3 (ROCKnrol-1) was discontinued after a pre-specified futility interim analysis; Tzield for delaying progression of stage 3 type 1 diabetes was under US priority review but not recommended for EU approval by the CHMP, and Sanofi decided not to progress the EU application at this time; Dupixent in eosinophilic gastritis (phase 3) and ulcerative colitis (phase 2) was deprioritized.
quarterly_data.figure: LEAP2MONO primary endpoints met; PERIDOT primary endpoint not met; ElevAATe and LIBERTY-AFRS-AI primary endpoints met; ROCKnrol-1 stopped for futility

quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory designations and other approvals in the 20-F pipeline tables: Wayrilz (rilzabrutinib) holds US orphan drug designation, plus US breakthrough therapy and Japan orphan drug designations (February 2026), in warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (phase 3 LUMINA 3), US orphan drug designation in sickle cell disease (phase 3 LIBRA), and US orphan drug, EU orphan and US fast track designations in IgG4-related disease (phase 3 RILIEF); efdoralprin alfa holds US orphan drug and EU orphan designations; SAR446268 (DMPK AAV gene therapy, phase 1 BrAAVe) holds US orphan drug designation in myotonic dystrophy type 1; Tzield received US priority review for young children. Approvals outside the US and EU: Dupixent in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in Japan, Sarclisa in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma in Japan and China, and Redemplo (plozasiran, RNAi targeting APOC3) in familial chylomicronemia syndrome in China (January 2026). New phase 3 programs include elenestinib (HARBOR) in indolent/smoldering systemic mastocytosis, and Qfitlia's Atlas NEO phase 3 supports EU and Japan submissions.
quarterly_data.figure: Wayrilz US breakthrough therapy designation (wAIHA) and US fast track (IgG4-RD); Redemplo approved in China January 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Beyfortus alliance: under the agreements Sanofi and AstraZeneca simplified in April 2023, Sanofi recognizes the sales and cost of sales (purchases of finished products from AstraZeneca) and shares the alliance's commercial profits with AstraZeneca; Sanofi could pay AstraZeneca up to EUR 375 million if sales objectives are met, and two payments of EUR 25 million and EUR 50 million were made in 2024 after contractual sales thresholds were reached. Beyfortus (RSV) sales were EUR 1,781 million in 2025 (+5.6%, +9.5% CER).
quarterly_data.figure: up to EUR 375 million sales-based payments to AstraZeneca; Beyfortus 2025 sales EUR 1,781 million
